headline: Count-based, uncertainty-aware and sequence models refine variant effects on expression and chromatin
label: Donor Aware Expression And Variant
summary: New preprints and papers pair personalised or count-based expression models with sequence predictors to score noncoding variants across cell types.
synthesis: The dominant thread is matching genetic-effect models to the structure of expression and chromatin data at the individual and cell-type level. jaxQTL fits negative binomial count models for pseudobulk sc-eQTL mapping and finds more eGenes than linear models, including distal ones. ATTICUS combines personalised sequence representations with uncertainty-aware prediction, transferring bulk pretraining to cell-type TWAS. A second strand evaluates sequence-based variant scoring: ChromBPNet models across 17 hematopoietic cell types score 302,830 noncoding variants with lineage-structured effects complementary to GWAS; ModBERT encodes variants and CpG methylation from long-read data; Evo2VED releases Evo2 scores for 6.48M gnomAD variants. The items are adjacent rather than one pipeline.
